title: Choose Class Finance’s visual world
question: Which dashboard direction should shape the modern Bendahara workspace? All options keep the Class Finance name, current logo, Indonesian wording, and existing finance workflows.

options.label: Meja Bendahara
options.lineage: A classroom treasurer’s labeled paper sorter
options.thesis: A quiet file index routes daily cash work into clear, named records.
options.viewport: A narrow persistent file index opens to a cash statement: available kas first, students and bills needing attention beside it, with recent transactions in a measured ledger below. The first glance answers how much cash is available and who still owes.
options.risk: If folder language becomes decoration, this will feel like stationery instead of a fast finance tool.

raised.raise: Align rupiah values and status columns to exact shared stops so every row can be compared at a glance.

options.label: Buku Kas Kelas
options.lineage: The class cash ledger and its daily closing balance
options.thesis: A living buku kas makes every incoming and outgoing rupiah easy to trace.
options.viewport: The dashboard reads like one current cash book: available balance, unpaid-bill summary, students needing follow-up, then a dated in/out ledger. Navigation stays quiet and familiar.
options.risk: Most familiar to finance users, but it may feel conventional if the ledger structure is too literal.

options.label: Kas Control Desk
options.lineage: A dark-first operations console with panels separated by precise seams
options.thesis: A deliberate workspace puts balances and overdue actions ahead of ornament.
options.viewport: Available kas and unpaid student balances lead the top panel; a compact attention queue and transaction list sit in clearly separated regions. Delete actions remain isolated and outlined.
options.case: Fuses as a clear finance control desk and protects destructive actions; it loses narrowly on Bendahara-specific identity.
options.risk: Could read as generic technical tooling, and a dark-first screen may be tiring for routine bookkeeping.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.case: Cosmic navigation does not help a Bendahara recognize class money or payment urgency.
options.kept: Vary marker size only when it encodes a real amount or priority.

options.label: Measured Type Grid
options.lineage: A Wim Crouwel grid-built type specimen
options.case: The poster-like typographic system makes letters more prominent than cash and bill status.
options.kept: Use a strict measured grid for amounts and status columns.

options.label: Payment Season Folio
options.lineage: A botanical sequence of changing states
options.case: A seasonal sequence obscures the immediate amount due and the next payment action.
options.kept: Make before and after payment states easy to compare.

options.label: Convention Index
options.case: A dense wall of tiny cells would slow student-by-student payment work.
options.kept: Keep navigation labels and student rows directly addressable.

options.label: Variable Type Specimen
options.lineage: An interactive foundry specimen with live type axes
options.case: Type controls add work without helping the Bendahara reconcile cash or dues.
options.kept: Keep numeric hierarchy stable and purposeful.

canonCard.label: The category-standard dashboard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar finance admin layout puts summary metrics above a student balance table.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional left navigation, a top balance summary, student payment statuses, and a recent transactions table.
canonCard.risk: Easy to scan, but visually similar to most admin dashboards.
